evidence.source: 李學勤主編,《字源》, 天津古籍出版社／遼寧人民出版社, 2012
evidence.field: 小 headword; PDF p. 76, printed p. 64; scanned headword and continuation checked on PDF p. 77, printed p. 65
evidence.text: The scanned entry identifies 小 as pictographic and interprets its marks as tiny grains of dust or sand, calling it an early graph of 沙; it says the graph was extended to mean ‘small,’ opposite 大, and gives that sense in oracle-bone and bronze inscriptions. It cites 《粹》1004 for 小雨, then describes extensions to low status, contempt, and youth. It says the current form was corrupted in bronze inscriptions and treats Shuowen’s 八-plus-丨 account as an explanation of that altered form. The adjacent 少 entry says 小 and 少 were originally one graph, with similar use in oracle-bone texts, and later differentiated; its explanation continues onto printed p. 65. Direct scan inspection confirms the cited headword and passage. Forms checked against pixels: 小, 少, 沙, 八, 丨, 大, and the text’s citation 《粹》1004. The scan supports what this author asserts; it does not settle the disputed sand-grain interpretation.
evidence.title: 《字源》 (2012), PDF pp. 76–77; printed pp. 64–65

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, Chinese University of Hong Kong
evidence.field: 小: formation, early use and adjacent 少 entry
evidence.text: The database reports two analyses of 小’s early marks: abstract dots for smallness, attributed to 商承祚 and 于省吾, or an early graph of 沙 depicting fine grains, attributed to 馬敘倫. It also describes 小 and 少 as an originally shared graph. Its examples include oracle-bone 小雨, time expressions 小食 and 小采, and bronze 小鼎, 小子 and 小臣. The page provides no absolute dates for these cited artifacts or usages, so it cannot alone establish a chronology among the senses.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：漢字甲骨部件分析—小

evidence.source: 金真姬,《常用漢字二百字探源》
evidence.field: 小, 字形探源／字義探源, PDF pp. 20–21; printed pp. 26–27
evidence.text: The inspected entry reports disagreement about what the three dots represent, including raindrops, scattered objects or fine smallness. It favors an abstract indication of smallness and says later lengthened dots prompted Shuowen’s 八-plus-丨 analysis, which it rejects as based on the altered form. It cites oracle-bone 小雨, 小風 and 小牢 as uses for ‘small.’ This supports a competing scholarly account, not a settled referent for the dots.
evidence.title: 《常用漢字二百字探源》, PDF pp. 20–21

evidence.source: 中央研究院, Academia Sinica Character Database
evidence.text: The page states that 少 and 小 were originally one graph depicting fine sand grains, with ‘small’ as the original meaning; it says the lower dot of 少 became a diagonal stroke in bronze inscriptions, distinguishing it from 小. This is an explicit shared-origin analysis, while other consulted sources retain competing analyses of 小’s dots.
evidence.title: 漢字「少」：字形演變

gaps: 字源’s claim that 小’s marks depict sand grains and that 小 was an early graph of 沙 is this author’s analysis; consulted references also support an abstract smallness-sign account. The original depicted referent remains unsettled. No inspected source establishes a phonetic borrowing of 沙 based on the name or pronunciation of depicted sand grains.

The 字源 entry reports oracle-bone 小雨 and other early meanings, but the underlying inscriptions were not inspected here; no absolute artifact dates or demonstrated semantic bridge for the time and status uses were established.
字源 PDF page 76 is printed p. 64; its continuation is PDF page 77, printed p. 65. Both scan images were directly inspected. No specific OCR correction was identified in the cited 小 passage.

The local reading row for 小 is current kMandarin metadata, not evidence about ancient sound relationships. The official individual Unicode Unihan record endpoint was not accessed in this research invocation.

The CUHK page attributes a sound role to 小 in 雀, but this invocation did not independently establish a historical sound relationship using inspected component and host readings in the same reconstruction system. Keep that role source-attributed and unresolved.
